A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UnrealZoo. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulator-speed benchmarks, navigation experiments, and tracking evaluations covering training diversity, crowds, control frequency and robot-dog transfer.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds comparator evaluations, navigation SPL scores, detailed simulator-speed measurements and cross-platform tracking experiments.

M1.justification: Figures 13–14 shorten the reported GPT-4o inference prompts, removing tracking heuristics and navigation action examples and validation instructions. UnrealZoo/UnrealCV+ components and the A3C/CQL architectures and losses otherwise match. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun using the revised prompts.

E1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds tracking in ThreeDWorld's Suburb Scene 2023 with a Magnebot target and physical-robot tracking of a person following an S-shaped path among distractors. These extend evaluation beyond UnrealZoo into another simulator and the real world. Robot-dog transfer and the four representative social-tracking environments already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds PID and fine-tuned OpenVLA to tracking comparisons. Robot-dog comparisons expand from offline RL alone to PID, GPT-4o, OpenVLA and RL in Table 5. The original comparisons among RL agents trained in one, two and eight environments remain in the appendices.

E3.justification: Navigation evaluation adds SPL. Table 5 changes from DowntownWest with 4/8/10 distractors to averages over four environments with 0/4/10 distractors; the appendix retains the earlier four-environment crowd protocol. New transfer experiments use EL/SR in ThreeDWorld and pixel deviation/IoU in physical deployment. These are different evaluation conditions, not directly comparable performance updates.

E4.justification: Appendix D.4 adds a transfer analysis comparing policies trained in one versus eight environments across another simulator and physical deployment, testing whether diversity benefits survive these domain shifts. Crowd and cross-embodiment analyses gain additional methods. The original training-diversity, control-frequency and learning-curve analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new physical-robot evaluation specifies five trials per policy. Existing 50-episode evaluations and the human benchmark's ten participants with five attempts each are unchanged. No new confidence intervals, significance tests or seed-based uncertainty estimates are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds SPL, including RL scores of 0.10 on Roof and 0.31 on Industrial Area, while retaining EL/SR values. New results include the revised Table 5 comparisons, per-environment FPS in Table 6, and transfer results in Table 15; ThreeDWorld EL/SR is 377/0.65 versus 493/0.80 for one- versus eight-environment training. v1 Tables 11–12 are numerically unchanged as v2 Tables 13–14.

T1.justification: The navigation and tracking reward equations and associated task definitions in Appendix B remain unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs. The additional evaluation metrics do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the diverse UnrealZoo environment collection, optimized UnrealCV+ interfaces, and evidence concerning environmental diversity, latency and difficult terrain. v2 foregrounds cross-embodiment difficulties already reported in v1 and adds supporting transfer evidence without materially redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: v1's dedicated Section 4.4 analysis of RL obstacle handling and GPT-4o response delays is removed. v2 adds PID occlusion and OpenVLA error-accumulation explanations, explicitly characterizes interactions as animation-based, and expands limitations to predefined object interactions and basic social dynamics. Appendix D.4 also adds interpretations of cross-platform generalization.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies FPS benchmark hardware, Windows OS, 640×480 resolution and 1,000 API calls, and adds an explicit UnrealZoo Gym repository address. Conversely, Figures 12–14 omit animal/drone configuration details and substantial prompt guidance. Existing RL hyperparameters, demonstration budgets and human-evaluation instructions are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to navigation evaluation by Anderson et al., SpatialVLM and OpenVLA. It also relates animation-based interactions to VirtualHome and discusses simulator customization when motivating ThreeDWorld transfer. The broader simulator comparison and research positioning remain substantially the same.

P1.justification: The abstract, related-work discussion, experimental narrative and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Experiment headings are reframed, Section 4.4 disappears, demonstration collection moves from Appendix B.4 to C.1, and a contents page and separate limitations appendix are introduced.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout with extensive figure and table relocation. The scene-distribution chart moves into the main text, entity-view images are rearranged and labeled, Tables 3–4 are transposed, and configuration/prompt displays are redesigned. New FPS and transfer displays are added, while the simulator-comparison table is duplicated in the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful comparator coverage, SPL, transfer experiments and FPS documentation. However, its new real-world Table 15 reports AD/IoU as 764/328 and 833/393 without explaining IoU scaling; the increased deviation also complicates Appendix D.4's claim of improved tracking. Together with shortened prompt and configuration disclosures, these unresolved reporting issues prevent a reliable judgment that the expanded evidence produces a net quality improvement.
